analysis.summary: Historical fix for drop elaboration of lint-only drops used by the Edition-2024 `tail_expr_drop_order` lint. Lint drops must be a distinct `DropKind::ForLint`, not a `Value` drop carrying a `backwards_incompatible_lint` boolean. On normal exits they emit only `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint`; on unwind paths and inside coroutines they must be handled with lint/storage semantics so the unwind drop tree does not perform a real `drop` for a lint-only local and the coroutine transform does not ICE.
analysis.originalLogic: `DropData` represented a lint-only drop as `kind: DropKind::Value` plus a separate `backwards_incompatible_lint: bool`. In `build_scope_drops`, a `Value` node with that bool set emitted only a `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` and did not build a real `Drop` terminator, but the drop tree construction and other consumers still saw the node as a value drop. `needs_cleanup` only considered `DropKind::Value`, and coroutine cleanup only had a `DropKind::Storage` arm.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is to keep a lint-only drop classified as a real value drop (or otherwise route it through the `DropKind::Value` unwind/coroutine handling) instead of a distinct `ForLint` kind. When that lint-only node is present on an unwind path, the unwind drop tree can emit a real `drop(place)` for a local whose normal-path behavior is only `backward incompatible drop(place)`; when lint/storage nodes are emitted on unwind, `unwind_to` must be advanced even though lint drops are normally omitted from unwind; and coroutine handling that only matches `DropKind::Storage` misses `ForLint` and can ICE while emitting the lint hint.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR produced by `ElaborateDrops` for Rust functions and async coroutines that contain values with custom `Drop` implementations in tail-expression/scope-exit positions subject to the Edition-2024 `tail_expr_drop_order` lint, especially when scope exit occurs on an unwind path (panic/cleanup) or inside a coroutine. The same source can be elaborated with the lint-only node treated as a value drop versus as `ForLint`; the observable difference is the MIR around normal and cleanup blocks, not the source program.
analysis.trigger: A `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint`/`ForLint` drop node is present at a scope exit that also has unwind cleanup, or the lint hint is emitted inside an async/coroutine body.
preconditions: The code is compiled with the Edition 2024 `tail_expr_drop_order` lint active (e.g. `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`).
A value with a custom destructor is dropped as a tail-expression temporary whose drop order changes in Rust 2024.
The scope exit can unwind (panic/cleanup path), or the code is an async/coroutine where cleanup indices are computed.
ElaborateDrops is run and its MIR is inspected (mir-opt test).
pitfalls: Do not model a lint-only drop as a real `DropKind::Value` drop: on unwind paths that can become an actual `drop(place)` instead of only `backward incompatible drop(place)`.
Do not forget to advance `unwind_to` for a `ForLint` node when `storage_dead_on_unwind` is true; lint drops are normally omitted on unwind, but not always.
Continue to skip the hint for moved locals on non-unwind paths, while not disturbing the unwind-tree caching mechanism.
Use `DUMMY_SP` for the `Goto` source info of an unwind-path lint hint so debuginfo does not place breakpoints there.
`Scope::needs_cleanup` must count `DropKind::ForLint`, otherwise scopes containing only lint drops may be misclassified.
Coroutine cleanup-index construction must include `DropKind::ForLint` (alongside `Storage`); missing it causes an ICE when emitting the lint drop statement.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` test using `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` and `// EMIT_MIR ...ElaborateDrops.after.mir`, with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`, a custom-`Drop` guard, and a `match` on a `Result` from a panicking helper. Check the after-ElaborateDrops MIR for `backward incompatible drop(...)` and ensure lint-only locals are not given a real `drop(...)` on unwind. Add a `tests/ui/drop` async test with a loop/`await` and `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]` to verify the coroutine path produces the lint diagnostic and does not ICE.
evidence: Make sure we handle `backwards_incompatible_lint` drops appropriately in drop elaboration #134486
